Vibration of effects

Source: R/voe.R
voe.Rd

Summarises how estimates and p-values vary across the specifications of a multiverse, separately for each response x coefficient.

Usage

voe(
  x,
  xvar = "pcor",
  p.adjusted = NULL,
  q = c(0.01, 0.5, 0.99),
  type = c("additive", "ratio"),
  null = 0,
  alpha = 0.05,
  decompose_variance = FALSE,
  focal = NULL,
  which.response = NULL,
  focal.var = NULL,
  p = NULL
)

Arguments

x

a pima object, a pima.multi object created with fit.specs, a list of fitted lm or glm models, or a table returned by spec_table().

xvar

column of the specification table to summarise (e.g. "pcor", "estimate").

p.adjusted

which p-values to use, with the same rules as spec_curve(): for pima objects TRUE uses the adjusted p-values, FALSE the unadjusted flipscores ones and NULL (default) the adjusted ones when pima() applied a correction; for lists of models and pima.multi objects only the unadjusted Wald p-values exist ("wald.p") and TRUE is an error.

q

probabilities for the quantiles; the extremes define the amplitudes and the Janus effect.

type

"additive" (difference) or "ratio" (exp of the difference, only with xvar = "estimate").

null

value under the null hypothesis on the scale of xvar (0 for estimate, pcor and z).

alpha

significance level.

decompose_variance

if TRUE, adds voe_variance().

focal, focal.var

coefficients and variables to consider, as in spec_curve(); by default the tested coefficients (pima), the focal predictors (pima.multi) or all the coefficients except the intercept. Each selected coefficient is a separate association.

which.response

responses to consider; defaults to all.

p

column of p-values of the specification table (e.g. one added with stats::p.adjust()). If NULL, chosen with the rules of p.adjusted.

Value

An object of class pima_voe: a list with summary (one row per response x coefficient), quantiles (long format), the settings used and, optionally, variance.

Details

Let \(x_s\) be the value of xvar and \(p_s\) the p-value of specification \(s\), \(Q_q\) the \(q\)-th quantile across the specifications and \(q_1 < q_2\) the extremes of q. For each association the function returns the quantiles of \(x_s\) and of \(-\log_{10} p_s\), the amplitudes $$x_{\mathrm{voe}} = Q_{q_2}(x) - Q_{q_1}(x), \qquad p_{\mathrm{voe}} = Q_{q_2}(-\log_{10} p) - Q_{q_1}(-\log_{10} p)$$ (p_voe is the relative p-value of Patel et al. (2015) ), and the Janus effect definitions (see janus()).

type = "ratio" requires xvar = "estimate": the ratio of the extreme quantiles of exp(estimate) equals exp() of their difference on the link scale (the relative hazard or odds ratio of Patel et al. (2015) ), that is \(\exp(x_{\mathrm{voe}})\). It is interpretable only for log, logit and cloglog links. Quantiles are always returned on the scale of xvar.

References

Patel CJ, Burford B, Ioannidis JPA (2015). “Assessment of Vibration of Effects due to Model Specification Can Demonstrate the Instability of Observational Associations.” Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 68(9), 1046–1058. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2015.05.029 .

See also

Other vibration of effects: janus(), voe_variance(), volcano()

Examples

multi <- create_multi(
  Sepal.Width ~ Sepal.Length + Petal.Width + Species,
  data = iris,
  focal = "Sepal.Length",
  nfuns = "log",
  fit.specs = list(lm = lm)
)
voe(multi)
#> Vibration of effects (xvar = pcor, type = additive, p-values = wald.p, alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#>     response  coefficient n_spec x_voe p_voe J_range J_pct J_ext J_sig J_frac
#>  Sepal.Width Sepal.Length      6 0.623  10.3    TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  0.833
voe(multi, xvar = "estimate", decompose_variance = TRUE)
#> Vibration of effects (xvar = estimate, type = additive, p-values = wald.p, alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#>     response  coefficient n_spec x_voe p_voe J_range J_pct J_ext J_sig J_frac
#>  Sepal.Width Sepal.Length      6 0.394  10.3    TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  0.833
#> 
#> Variance decomposition:
#>     response  coefficient        term    source   r2u  pr2u r2u_inclusion
#>  Sepal.Width Sepal.Length Petal.Width predictor 0.295 0.607         0.279
#>  Sepal.Width Sepal.Length     Species predictor 0.191 0.393         0.191
#>  r2u_transformation
#>              0.0158
#>              0.0000
